newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks make modest gains at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks make modest gains at open.

text.p: The Australian sharemarket opened higher on Thursday with most of the leaders making modest gains.
The gold sector jumped 2.8 percent as the gold price rallied from its recent lows in overseas markets.
In the industrials, ANZ Bank went ex-dividend 24 (19 U.S.) cents, limiting gains in that sector.
Dividend related trading also boosted ANZ volumes, with 29 million shares traded prior to the official market opening.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index added 7.2 points to 2,377.9.
"It's a bit of a mixed bag," said dealer at a Brisbane brokerage.
"The golds seem to be reacting, maybe overreacting, to the rise in the (gold) price overnight and BHP having a bit of a bounce is helping the index."
While sounding a note of caution, the dealer pointed to recent heavy selling, adding that the lower Australian dollar as helping the bullion's resurgence.

"There has been pretty heavy selling in the last few weeks so people are maybe thinking the worst is over but I think it is a little bit early to call that. The dollar staying down under 80 cents is a positive for the miners," he said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about two to one, while about 43 percent of stocks traded remained steady. (A$1 = US$0.79)
